oracle: Independent circular first-match priority, post-grant rotation and payload routing model. It is derived from the arbitration contract and shares no structure with the kill chain, mask/priority encoder or wrapper output pipelines of the devices under test.

exhaustive: vc_FixedArbChain: every kill-in value crossed with every request vector for N in 1..5
vc_FixedArb: every request vector for N in 1..5
vc_VariableArbChain: every kill-in value crossed with every one-hot priority and every request vector for N in 1..5
vc_VariableArb: every one-hot priority crossed with every request vector for N in 1..5
vc_RoundRobinArbChain and vc_RoundRobinArb: every rotation state crossed with every request vector for N in 1..5, reached by a one-cycle steering grant
vc_RoundRobinArb_V2: every rotation pointer base crossed with every request vector for N in 1..5, reached by a two-cycle steering pair
wrappers: every non-empty request vector for N in 1..4
parameter_classes: N=1 degenerate arbiter on every primitive and every wrapper
round-robin chain reset priority index 0 and index N-1
backpressure: kill-in asserted before and after a grant on both arbiter chains
wrapper disabled while requests are held, then released
wrapper submit deasserted so the published payload is cleared
wrapper submit asserted by requesters that never win the arbitration
asynchronous reset asserted mid-cycle on every sequential module
stimulus.handshake_timing: Fan-in wrappers are driven with the pipeline the AFU actually uses: requests and the combinational grant in cycle t, ready in cycle t+1, and the granted requester's submit plus buffer data in cycle t+2. The model therefore gates publication with grant_latched, the delayed copy of the grant that caused the buffer pop, while ready keeps advertising the current winner.

assertions: grants equal the independent model every vector
a grant implies a request on the same index
kout equals request-or-kill-in on both arbiter chains
round-robin rotation advances to winner+1 only when a grant is taken
bounded fairness: every requester wins inside N cycles (2N for vc_RoundRobinArb_V2 whose registered grant blacks out the winner for one cycle)
wrapper ready equals the registered grant and stays one-hot
wrapper payload equals the buffer of the requester that owned the delayed grant, including when several requesters submit in the same cycle
a requester that never owned the delayed grant publishes nothing
wrapper payload and ready clear asynchronously on reset

characterized_behavior: round_robin_priority_arbiter_N_input_1_ouput gates the output register with a registered copy of `enabled`, so enable changes take effect one cycle later than in the fixed wrapper. This is a deliberate pipeline stage, not a defect: ready and arbiter_out stay mutually consistent because both are gated by the same registered enable, and the existing default latency is preserved. The 10 fan-in stall and 10 stall-release bins pin the behaviour, and the rr-fanin-enable-delay-removed mutation fails if it is quietly changed.

vc_RoundRobinArb_V2 registers its grant and masks it with the previous grant, so a continuously requesting client is granted at most every other cycle. Fairness is therefore checked against a 2N cycle window instead of N.

Both fan-in wrappers keep `requests` and `submit` as separate ports; the arbiter rotates on `requests` even while the wrapper is disabled, so grants taken during a stall are not replayed after release. A requester owes its data exactly one cycle after it sees ready; the wrapper publishes nothing if it never delivers.

production_fixes.defect: vc_RoundRobinArbChain, vc_RoundRobinArb and vc_RoundRobinArb_V2 could not elaborate at p_num_reqs = 1
production_fixes.detail: priority_next used grants[p_num_reqs-2:0], which degenerates to grants[-1:0], and vc_RoundRobinArb_V2 assigned rotate_ptr[1] unconditionally.
production_fixes.fix: The rotate expression and the rotate_ptr[1] register moved into generate branches, so the p_num_reqs = 1 elaboration contains no negative or out-of-range select. A single requester rotates onto itself, which keeps the one-hot priority invariant.
production_fixes.regression: RR_N now includes 1: 60 winner, 60 state, 20 fairness, 20 idle, 20 reset and 10 kill-in bins cover N=1 through N=5, and the rr-chain-single-rotation-broken and rr-arb-single-rotation-broken mutations only perturb the N=1 branch.

production_fixes.defect: fan-in wrappers published the highest submitter instead of the arbitration winner
production_fixes.detail: The payload loop assigned arbiter_out for every set submit bit, so with a multi-hot submit the last loop iteration won while ready still reported the grant.
production_fixes.fix: publish = grant & submit gates the payload with the one-hot grant; a losing submitter publishes nothing and the output clears.
production_fixes.regression: 8 grant-aligned multi-hot bins, 10 losing-submitter bins, and the fixed/rr fanin-publish-highest-submitter mutations.

production_fixes.defect: arbiter_out in the fan-out wrappers had no reset and leaked a stale payload
production_fixes.detail: The output register used always @(posedge clock) only, so a payload published before reset stayed visible on the destination port until a later clock edge.
production_fixes.fix: The register now uses always_ff @(posedge clock or negedge rstn) and clears every destination asynchronously.
production_fixes.regression: 10 fan-out reset payload-clear bins plus the fixed/rr fanout-reset-removed mutations.

production_fixes.detail: The signal was never driven and its only consumer was commented out, leaving 13 permanently unreachable toggle points.
production_fixes.fix: Declaration removed; the unreachable-point list shrank accordingly.

production_fixes.defect: fan-in wrappers published against the new combinational grant instead of the grant that caused the buffer pop
production_fixes.detail: The grant-aligned payload gate introduced with the multi-hot fix used the current cycle's grant. The AFU registers the arbiter's ready once more before it pops a command FIFO, and the FIFO drives data_out combinationally on that pop, so submit and buffer data arrive two cycles after the combinational grant. With round-robin the winner rotates every cycle, so the gate never matched and commands were dropped; run_integration.py failed the round-robin command count while fixed priority still passed because its winner is stable.
production_fixes.fix: publish = grant_latched & submit, where grant_latched is the registered copy of ready. ready still advertises the current winner, so arbitration latency and fairness are unchanged, and a multi-hot submit still cannot override the delayed winner.
production_fixes.regression: The unit testbench now drives submit and buffer data one cycle after ready. Four mutations pin the stage count: fixed/rr-fanin-publish-combinational-grant reproduce the integration failure exactly and fixed/rr-fanin-publish-undelayed-ready catch a one-stage error.
